newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ok Tedi copper shipments flow as rain fall in PNG.
newsitem.headline: Ok Tedi copper shipments flow as rain fall in PNG.

text.p: Ongoing rains have enabled the Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea to maintain shipments of copper concentrates on the Fly River this week, a spokesman for the mine's operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday.
"The river is still flowing," the spokesman said.

One of two grinding mills shut down last month as drought conditions worsened at the remote mine site in the Western Province of PNG has been restarted, although a second mill remains idle, the spokesman said.
There needs to be more lasting signs of an end to the drought before the second mill would be restarted, he said.
"At the moment, there is still no signs of any improvement in the drought," he said.
"We have been advised that we are still in for a long dry spell."

Shipments of concentrates resumed on Monday after heavy rains lifted the water level of the Fly River, which is normally used to ferry concentrates by barge from the Port of Kiunga to the mouth of the river for loading onto silo vessels.
However, because of recent drought conditions, the silo has been moved to Port Moresby harbour, extending the normally two-day journey to four days, the spokesman said.
Concentrates from Ok Tedi are sold mostly to smelters in Asia and Europe, although no shipments are currently scheduled, the spokesman said.
River traffic was first suspended on June 2.
At the peak of the drought, about 140,000-150,000 tonnes of concentrate stored at the Port of Kiunga.

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese Smelter Pool which consists of seven Japanese smelters. BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine.
The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
